idiom_name: goroutine + one-element channel (channel-as-future); context and errgroup for cancellation and fan-in
implementation_notes: Go has no Future type and the idiom that replaces the classic structure is a goroutine that sends its single result on a channel - a future is essentially a one-element channel and the promise is the sending goroutine - so the read end is a receive or a receive arm in a select next to ctx.Done(). Because channels carry only the value, deadlines and cancellation travel separately in a context.Context, and fan-in of several pending results with error propagation is written with sync.WaitGroup plus result/error channels (or x/sync/errgroup). The promise/future roles are thus absorbed into language primitives rather than classes, and a hand-written once-only result struct is only worth it when many callers must await the same pending value.
pitfalls: An unbuffered result channel plus a producer nobody receives from leaks the goroutine forever: buffer the single slot (make(chan T, 1)) or guarantee a drain, and give the goroutine a context so it can stop.
A goroutine is not tied to its starter: without context or errgroup, a caller that gives up leaves the work running and its error unobserved - the Go form of the dropped future.
Guarding a shared pending result with sync.Once and a struct field is easy to get subtly wrong (publication, error storage); prefer the channel or the errgroup when several consumers wait.
